items.statement: Launched FreightJar 2.0 with global access, real-time rates, better customer experience; hiring for this vertical
items.quote: we were able to finalize the Version 2 of our logistics online platform Freight Jar which will definitely give us better access to more markets and better access to more customers & clients who are dealing in the international business.

items.statement: Won government contracts including 1-year HPCL petrochemical logistics and BHEL ODC/container shipments
items.quote: Development of the government projects business, it's doing well for us. We've got some good contracts this quarter as well.

items.statement: Overall volume grew ~17% QoQ despite lowest-ever freight rates reducing FY24 revenue to ₹24,026 lakhs from ₹43,335 lakhs
items.quote: though maybe I may have a 15% increase, 17% increase in the overall volume, but my billing has gone down because the freight itself has come down. So that is the reason for that.

items.statement: FreightJar platform operates at same 7-8% margin as core business
items.quote: The revenue model is purely what we are doing now. Since it is a sales product of Tiger Logistics, we are offering the same services through the online portal. So, the margin remains the same at 7%-8% whatever is there in our business.

items.statement: High freight rates causing some low-value product importers to hold shipments short-term
items.quote: It's not come till now but yeah, people are holding their imports because the rates have gone up so high. So, they feel that it is better to hold on, not immediately, but that impact does come in.

items.statement: Inorganic growth via LCL acquisition pending due to lack of aligned targets
items.quote: the only thing which is lacking is that we were looking at some kind of inorganic growth in terms of acquiring LCL company, which has not happened because you know we were not able to get the company which is aligned to our idea of growth.

items.statement: Robust order book exceeding INR 40 crores
items.quote: With a diverse product portfolio of over 25 SKUs and a robust order book of exceeding INR 40 crores, we serve B2B customers across defense, marine, offshore, oil and gas and other industries.

items.statement: H2 FY24 EBITDA margin 24.96%, PAT margin 14.85%
items.quote: The EBITDA was INR 10.83 crore with a Meson Valves India Ltd 3 18.06.2024 Result Conference Call robust EBITDA margin of 24.96%, reflecting operational efficiency. The notable profit after tax PAT of INR 6.44 crores with a PAT margin of 14.85% further underscores Meson's financial strength

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 23.61%, PAT margin 14.3%
items.quote: The EBITDA was INR 4.95 crore with a strong EBITDA margin of 23.61%, indicating continuous operational efficiency. The PAT was INR 9.05 crore with a PAT margin of 14.3%, underscoring Meson's financial robustness.

items.statement: Targeting sustainable 25-30% year-on-year growth
items.quote: So I think we will be able to achieve a very sustainable growth of 25%, 30% year-on-year. So that is also our target to be sustainable.

items.statement: Present CapEx around INR 15 crores as of May 2024; FY25 CapEx in planning
items.quote: Present we have around 15 CR CapEx. So we are planning yeah. Yeah. We are planning to have some more machineries, technological machine s and equipment in future so we can enhance our productivity also with the new technologies we will have increase in the ROCE

items.statement: Foundry integration and new CNC machines to increase throughput by 30-40%
items.quote: So, yeah. I can say if you just put it in numbers literally, it will be 30%, 40% increase.

items.statement: Foundry backward integration may add 3% to PAT margin once fully operational
items.quote: It is possible that the foundry will add to somewhere shares increase the margin, I think, by 3%. It is possible. Yes.

items.statement: 50-60% of revenues expected from defense sector
items.quote: 50-60% revenues will come only from defense.

items.statement: Huge surge in domestic shipbuilding and naval projects; capacity utilization was 100% for domestic demand
items.quote: Even in the coming future, we see a huge demand from the Indian local PSUs with the defense maritime, marine and as the things are progressing, we see that there is a huge surge in the local domestic shipbuilding projects, naval projects, where we have to also significantly gear up.

items.statement: H2O Dynamics water treatment venture receiving 20-25 inquiries, expecting conversion
items.quote: What I want to add that we just started, but the response from the industry is very much overwhelming, like we are getting we almost got 20, 25 inquiries right now. And most of the inquiries we are seeing that we can convert into the business.

items.statement: German filter technology for automatic cleaning; 80% Make in India, 20% parts from Germany
items.quote: Make in India. And some parts, say, around 20% parts will come from Germany, 80% of it will be made in India.

items.statement: Seasonality trend H1/H2 30-70% or 40-60% to continue for couple of years due to consolidation
items.quote: So it always it will be a trend for at least a couple of years. Once you are at a particular level, once your things are great, things are in auto mode, then this trend start, this trend becomes both the quarters become try to equalize.

items.statement: Nibe Meson Naval JV full management in place from September; revenue expected H2
items.quote: The JV, the management will be in place from September. items.quote: There are better margins, but the valves to make the nonferrous metal is very critical. However, we have that technology, we have our need and developed. So we have that technology, so we have the edge

items.quote: I don't think, at this point in time, we can give any outlook or guidance on growth. The thing is RBI ban has to be lifted. So, our focus will be in compliance this year and the complia nce, risk management and control. So, there's no guidance for growth that we can give

items.quote: So that is about approximately INR272 crores in the gold loan and that has resulted in the spike in gold loan GNPA and which I think will normalize in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Home loan disbursements normalized to Q1 FY24 levels; growth expected in coming quarters
items.quote: In the home finance, we are seeing that the growth is, the disbursements has normalized. They are at a level maybe similar to what it was in the first quarter of last year. Maybe, and then going forward in the next few quarters, we'll see growth as the environment also has become positive.

items.quote: In terms of our operating cost which again in Q4 till the RBI order came we were on a growth path and particularly our microfinance business was also on an aggressive hiring spree for th e branches that were set up in the quarter before. And March quarter typically also is a higher volume and higher cost as well in terms of the incentive bonuses which have been committed or approved, they are also

items.statement: No retrenchment; maintaining gold loan infrastructure at INR360 crores quarterly running cost
items.quote: So gold loan, our standalone running cost is around the INR360 crores in a quarter, which is around INR120 crores per month. But that includes the top management cost as well as business loan. And significant part of that cost is difficult to separate. So that is one thing.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM down from over INR26,000 crores to below INR16,000 crores; INR10,000+ crores repaid
items.quote: But what is really heartening and what is really positive for us to note that our loan book which was around over INR26,000 crores on the 4th March has come down a little below INR16,000 crores currently and more than INR10,000 crores of gold loans have been repaid by the customers and they've taken their jewellery and we did not have any case of customer disgruntled or any asset quality issue or

items.quote: But cost-to-income ratio may remain a little more elevated because our gold loan book has run down. And obviously, the income that we get, the net interest margin, which we are getting, say, on INR26,000 crores on March and actually would have grown further in the month of March will be significantly lower.

items.statement: Quarterly average cost of borrowing increased 20 bps YoY and 6 bps QoQ to 9.13%
items.quote: Our quarterly average cost of borrowing has increased by 20 basis point Y-o-Y and 6 basis point to 9.13 as on 31st of March.

items.statement: Special audit completed; report submitted to RBI; engaging positively for ban lift
items.quote: The special audit has completed, and special auditors have submitted the report to RBI. In terms of, as far as the company is concerned, we are very confident that we are fully complied with all the regulations of RBI as well as we have addressed all the deficiencies.

items.statement: Fair value loss of INR200 crores from AIF unit expiry and ARC SR markdowns (one-off)
items.quote: Other than that, I think there's a INR200 crores of loss in a fair value. items.statement: Raised INR5,531 crores in Q4 FY24 including INR1,271 crores rights issue and INR500 crores NCD; cash INR6,559 crores

Prominent among them was INR1,271 crores that we raised through the rights issue in May and INR500 crores that we raised through the NCD that we borrowed in the month of March. Our cash and cash equivalents stands at around INR6,559 crores.

items.quote: Talking about the AUM for the quarter consolidated AUM grew by 22% on a Y-o-Y basis and 2% on a quarter-on-quarter basis to around INR78,960 crores. items.statement: Plan to add ~40,000 new seats in FY25 reaching ~135,000 total seats by end of FY25
items.quote: We plan to add around ~40,000 new seats in FY25 reaching a total of ~135,000 seats by end of FY25.

items.statement: Expect to grow revenue by 30% in FY25
items.quote: We expect to grow our revenue by 30% in FY25.

items.statement: Expect to improve EBITDA margins by approximately 1.5% for FY25 versus FY24
items.quote: Due to an increase in occupancy and operating leverage on costs, we should be able to improve our EBITDA margins by approximately 1.5% for FY25 versus FY24.

items.statement: Capex spends for FY25 expected in a very similar range to FY24's INR142 crores
items.quote: Our capex spends excluding the right of use assets for FY24 stood at INR142 crores while for FY25 we expect capex spends in a very similar range.

items.statement: As of March 24, approximately 15,500 seats in fit-outs and approximately 16,500 seats with signed LOI
items.quote: As of March 24, we already have approximately 15,500 seats in the fit outs and for approximately 16,500 seats we have signed LOI in place.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin at 31%, Q4 FY24 at 31.5%; IND-AS 116 adjusted EBITDA improved to 10.4% in FY24 from 4.3% in FY23
items.quote: The margins stood at 31% for FY24 and at 31.5% for Q4 FY24.

items.statement: Target center EBITDA margins: 30-35% for Straight Lease, 23-25% for Managed Aggregation at >85% stable occupancy
items.quote: the ideal margin for straight-leave centers for us ve ry, between 30 % to 35 %. This is the center EBITDA margin. And for the managed aggregation centers, closer to about 23% to ~25% is the center EBITDA margin

items.statement: Pricing per seat per month ranges from INR6,000 to INR18,000; escalations of 4-6% for larger cohorts, 5-8% for smaller cohorts on existing contracts
items.quote: Our pricing of the product on a per se at basis ranges from about INR6,000 to INR18,000 per seat per month.

items.statement: Industry seat take-up growing at ~42% CAGR, expected to reach 335,000-345,000 seats/year by 2026; flexible workspace penetration to rise to 16% by 2026
items.quote: The year -on-year seat take-up is increasing at a CA GR of approximately 42% from approximately 59,000 to 69,000 seats per year in 2019 to 1,67,000 seats to 1,77,000 seats per year in 2022 and expected to reach 3,35,000 seats to 3,45,000 seats per year by 2026.

items.statement: Revenue mix to remain ~75% co-working, ~20-25% design & build (Awfis Transform); Transform margins currently 14-15%, targeting +1.5% improvement in FY25
items.quote: We will continue to have about 75% of our business in co-working and about similar about 20%-25% in design and build.

items.statement: No foreseen challenges in sourcing Managed Aggregation supply given brand credibility, landlord returns delivered, and 350-400 broker partners
items.quote: With this brand we have, with the credibility we have built, with the returns we have delivered to our landlords, we don't foresee any challenges.

items.statement: IPO of INR599 crores completed (INR129 crores fresh issue); net proceeds for capex, working capital, general corporate purposes
items.quote: We recently concluded our IPO of INR 599 crores through a combination of fresh issue of INR129 crores and an offer for sale of INR 471 crores by selling shareholders.

items.statement: Managed Aggregation model share increased from 46% of seats in FY21 to 66% in FY24; target to maintain 65-68% MA mix
items.quote: Our endeavor would be to continue the split as we have been able to achieve which is approximately 65% to 68% of MA, Managed Aggregation and the rest being Straight Lease.

items.statement: Corporate overheads (HO staff) at 5-6% of total revenues; ESOP expense pool ~INR6 crores unamortized over FY25-26
items.quote: The corporate overhead for that cost gets distributed between the landlord and us. On the other corporate overhead, which is the salary for the HO staff is in the range of 5%-6%.

items.statement: Cash EBIT (EBITDA less actual lease payments) was INR97 crores in FY24, up 168% YoY; March 2024 monthly run-rate ~INR9.5 crores
items.quote: Cash EBIT number for FY '24 is INR97 crores to be precise. And the way we calculate the cash EBIT is EBITDA less than the actual lease payments.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs 550 crore for FY25, implying over 30% growth from FY24
items.quote: Eventually, if we are targeted from 423 to 550, so it's almost over 30% growth.

items.statement: Capex planned at Rs 60 crore for FY25, primarily for future projects like Project Titan
items.quote: Total investment is For plan for this year is 60 crores and out of this substantial portion is going to be invested further titen project

items.statement: Project Titan (parking lock mechanism for German OEM) functional build samples expected by July end, series production line build in Feb 2025, mass production start by Aug 2026
items.quote: The functional build samples for assembly trials at the customer lines. It is expected by July end, then the next build phase on series production line is planned in February 2025 and then everything if everything goes off well then we are expecting the start of the mass production last by August 2026.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 20-23% range for FY25 as scale grows
items.quote: We have always maintained that you know as our business will grow as they con as the scale of operations will grow and all. Our EBITDA margin should be in the range of 20 to 23% and all.

items.statement: European demand showing slight slowdown and stock correction, but new launches and new projects expected to sustain growth
items.quote: There's a little Weakening of the demands. I'll not say it decline, but the beginning of the demand or it's a little stock correction also because in COVID time everybody over produced in Europe and the US Now they're taking care of the stock corrections also these multiple effects are there, but we are safe because we are always having new launches, new products, so.

items.statement: ZF business started 1-1.5 years ago, projected to grow to double-digit percentage of revenue, advanced discussions on new resourcing projects
items.quote: ZF is going to be one of our biggest customer. The business only started a year back, year and a half back. items.quote: You know, we lost almost 40 crores of sale in last year because postpaid. Yeah, it was postponed or delayed postponed and Eventually, out of this you can say around 40% sale was on account of This game landing loss here.

items.statement: Long-term debt repayment of ~Rs 48 crore scheduled for FY25; overall debt reduction targeted despite growth capex
items.quote: Close to close to 48 crores.

items.statement: Revenue target revised to INR6,000-6,500 crores by FY27 with 3-4% PAT margin and 25% ROCE
items.quote: We are looking to achieve INR6,000 crores revenue, 3% to 4% PAT margin and of 25% ROCE.

items.statement: Export revenue share to increase from low double-digits to 30% by FY27
items.quote: We expect revenues from export business to increase quite significantly as a percentage of total revenues over the years from the current contribution of low double-digits to 30% by FY '27.

items.statement: Acquired entities expected to generate INR600-650 crores revenue and INR15-17 crores PAT in FY25
items.value: INR600-650 crores revenue, INR15-17 crores PAT
items.quote: During 2025, we expect both entities to generate INR600 crores to INR650 crores of revenue and a PAT of INR15 crores to INR17 crores.

items.statement: Existing factory with minimal capex can support over INR5,000 crores revenue; current capacity 750 kg/month at Sky Gold plus 200-300 kg/month at acquired entities
items.quote: Our existing factory alone with minimal investment in capital expenditure can let us grow more than INR5,000 crores in revenues.

items.statement: Targeting 3% PAT margin initially, then 3-4% in three years driven by interest cost reduction and ERP implementation
items.quote: First target is to achieve 3% PAT margins. In three years, we will be ranging about 3%-4%.

items.statement: Gross margin structurally 7-8% through product mix and exports; EBITDA margin maintained at 5-5.5% long term
items.quote: Structurally, we would like to reach 7% to 8% gross margins through product mix and exports. EBITDA margin would be maintained at 5-5.5 over the long term.

items.statement: Interest costs to drop by more than half to under 0.5% of sales by shifting 80-90% to gold metal loans at 3% and liquidating equity collateral for FD income
items.quote: As a result of conversation from working capital loan to GML and liquidation of shares, our interest costs would more than drop by half to less than 0.5% of the sales.

items.statement: Domestic organized retail expanding rapidly with 500 new stores from top 5 chains in 3-5 years; unorganized market share shifting from 65% to 35%
items.quote: India's large retail jewellery chains are expanding at a breakneck speed, with estimates suggesting 500 new stores coming up from just five top chains in the next three to five years.

items.quote: strategically decided to enter a diamond-studded jewellery segment driven by the high demand for such products, particularly in the lightweight category where we are market leaders

items.statement: Gold price volatility factored into guidance assuming 8-9% annual increase; no slowdown seen in Q1 despite price rise and elections due to Akshaya Tritiya demand
items.quote: Yearly 8% to 9% gold prices increases on average. The data says that. So, we have calculated both.

items.statement: No external capital needed for next two years; will raise at appropriate time when board approves plan
items.quote: One year, at present there is no need for external capital. We would take capital at the appropriate time that whenever board is comfortable and agree the plan and we will plan that out.

items.quote: To simplify the transaction further, the total acquisition cost is INR87.5 crores that is INR49.98 crores of shares and INR37.5 crores of repayable loans through cash and equity components.

items.statement: Gold metal loan adoption at 6-7% currently; targeting 25% this quarter, 75-80% next quarter, 100% in two quarters

items.statement: ERP system to be operational in next few months; targeting cash conversion cycle reduction to 45 days over two years
items.quote: Over the next two years, we would like to lower the capital cycle to 45 days.

items.statement: Hired operations head with 25 years US/Europe experience; developing 14/18 carat products for Western markets over two quarters
items.quote: We have hired an operations head which has experience of 25 years of US and Europe market. Recently we have hired him for this project and we are building a team.
